grh_c50e7a09b46314485465.title: Antiques
paragraphs: The proud Proctor sisters live in an old family mansion filled with heirlooms, but bedridden Jane does not realize how badly their finances have collapsed. Her sister Libby has been quietly selling treasured family pieces one by one to keep the household going, even parting with a desk that had belonged to their father and grandfather. Dr. Christian recognizes the desk in an antique shop and understands why Libby refused to open the mansion for a Red Cross tour and why she has become increasingly desperate. Rather than expose the secret to Jane, he finds a way to give the house a useful new life: Mrs. Dawson, the wife of a serviceman, and her two children desperately need room while the husband is away. Christian persuades the Proctors to take the family in, giving Jane companionship and purpose, bringing children and life back into the mansion, and easing the pressure that had been forcing Libby to sacrifice the family's past piece by piece.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on November 25, 1942. It is listed as episode 209 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt, Nancy Evans, Regina Wallace, Horace Willard, and Ann Stone.
The surviving recording runs about 24 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_c556dc66b8cf782d18e6.title: Hollywood Visitor
paragraphs: Fading Hollywood star Madeline Kay visits the English coastal home of her financial adviser Charles and bluntly tells his wife that she intends to take him away from her. Local fishermen try to warn Charles that something dangerous is moving in the water, but he dismisses them and takes Madeline out by boat. A gigantic octopus-like creature attacks; the fishermen rescue Charles and the others, but the monster finally coils an arm around Madeline and drags her into the sea, turning the story’s warning about retribution into a literal ending.
